title: Backcasting probe-guided refusal vs flat refusal: does steering give finer control than a blanket refusal switch?

original_idea.body: Graded vs binary refusal steering idea

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Graded refusal reduces over-refusal on dual-use prompts (plausible chain) but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Compare hard-threshold vs graded steering; guided but building a dual-use prompt set and two interventions adds effort.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused head-to-head deliverable with a few dependencies (probe + steering + sensitive prompt set).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open weights, no lab access; over-refusal is a diffuse problem labs underweight, independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Fine-grained refusal steering exists; the graded-vs-binary head-to-head may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Fine-grained refusal steering exists; the explicit graded-vs-binary tradeoff comparison may be open.
